title: Ensure scanners are in place to identify and prevent sensitive data in code
description: A secret pushed to a repository is exposed to everyone who can read it, and stays in its history after the fix. GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps can reject a push that contains a secret — the only server-side prevention Azure Repos offers. It is a paid add-on available on Azure DevOps Services only; elsewhere this control needs a person.
remediation: Project settings -> Repositories -> <repository> -> Settings -> Advanced Security: turn on Secret Protection, and "Block secrets on push". Organization settings -> Repositories can turn it on for every repository, and for new ones automatically. On Azure DevOps Server, which has no Advanced Security, run a secret scanner as a required build validation instead and review this control by hand.
fixSummary: Turn on "Block secrets on push" at Project settings -> Repositories -> <repo> -> Settings.
